convention: anthropics/skills/skill-creator evals.json — two kinds. `kind:"trigger"` fixtures carry `should_trigger` for description-optimisation (train/held-out trigger accuracy). `kind:"behavioural"` fixtures carry a `tier` (M/D/R) and `expectations[]` asserting the skill applies / reasons / declines correctly on a Reagent→Freehand fixture input.
notes: Positives target Reagent-view→Freehand prompts on an already-re-frame2 app (v/defview, deref-drop, moving off Reagent hiccup). Negatives target the DIFFERENT v1→v2 events/subs/db migration (re-frame-migration), authoring on re-frame2 (re-frame2), greenfield (re-frame2-setup), live runtime (re-frame2-pair), and the first-class 'stay on Reagent' non-goal. Behavioural fixtures cover the M/D/R tiers, and several exist specifically to catch the failure mode of emitting a Freehand verb that is described in the design corpus but not exported (local, effect, ref, a trusted-markup form; the outward React bridge v/->react was once such a gap and has since shipped, so it is verified against the live roster rather than assumed absent).

evals.name: m-transform-defview-sub-lift
evals.prompt:
Convert this to Freehand, and write a structural test that asserts the converted price view shows the cart total:
(defn price [amt cur] [:button {:on-click #(dispatch [:buy amt])} @(subscribe [:total])])
(defn app [] [:div [price 1 2]])
expectations: Rewrites the header to (v/defview price [{:keys [amt cur]}] ...) — positional params become one destructured props map (MIG-01).
Declares the props parameter on the zero-prop view as [_], never [] — a zero-arity defview raises :rf.error/defview-bad-args at macro-expansion.
Rewrites the call site atomically to [price {:amt 1 :cur 2}] in the same change (MIG-01).
Drops the deref: @(subscribe [:total]) becomes (v/sub [:total]) (MIG-02).
Lifts the handler: {:on-click #(dispatch [:buy amt])} becomes {:on-click [:buy amt]} (MIG-04).
Adds the require [re-frame.freehand :as v] (MIG-24) and cites the MIG ids for each change.
Does NOT treat the event vector [:buy amt] or the query vector [:total] as hiccup to respell/spread.
Does NOT add {:compiled true} — a migration pass emits interpreted declarations.

Writes the requested structural test: requires [re-frame.freehand.test :as t], drives state under an rf/with-new-frame + rf/dispatch-sync bracket, and renders the now v/sub-reading price body inside (t/with-render (t/render [price {:amt 1 :cur 2}])).

Uses the with-render bracket for that state-reading render — a bare (t/render [price …]) of a v/sub-reading view raises :rf.error/view-read-outside-render, so an answer whose test renders bare is WRONG and only the (t/with-render (t/render …)) form passes.

evals.name: d-decide-form2-local-state
evals.prompt:
Migrate this Reagent view to Freehand:
(defn dropdown [] (r/with-let [open? (r/atom false)] [:div {:on-click #(reset! open? true)} (when @open? [:ul])]))
expectations: Recognises Form-2 / with-let view-held state (MIG-16) and does NOT silently rewrite the view.
States that Freehand has no `local` — there is no host-local cell to translate the r/atom into — and does not emit one.

Reasons about the real decision: product state → app-db (an event + a sub, a dataflow change to name for the author); a control owning a genuine multi-interaction protocol → a semantic controller; DOM-owned state → a registered behavior.
For a simple open/closed flag, lands on app-db rather than treating 'it's only ephemeral' as a reason to keep it in the view.
Holds the WHOLE view until the decision is made (cardinal rule 2), rather than converting some sites and leaving others.
Does not reach into the dataflow layer itself; it names the reg-event/reg-sub for the author when app-db is the answer.

evals.name: d-route-ssr-static-vs-hydrate
evals.prompt:
Migrate this to Freehand:
(ns app.render (:require [reagent.dom.server :as s]))
(defn render-page [] (s/render-to-string [app]))
expectations: Routes the STATIC-page arm of MIG-23 to (v/render-static [app-root {}]) — the pure :server-phase render, Freehand's counterpart of renderToStaticMarkup — NOT a decline.
Notes render-static is a MACRO (the root form is literal) and JVM/server only, and that day8/re-frame2-ssr must be on the classpath at render time.
Notes there is no silent elision: a runtime-requiring capability in the server-reachable closure is a loud build error with source coordinates, not a dropped capability.
For SSR-then-hydrate, names re-frame.ssr/hydrate! (seed state) then v/hydrate-root (adopt the DOM), and that identity opts are refused client-side because identity comes from the server.
Verifies the author's server pipeline against re-frame.ssr's actual exports rather than assuming a helper exists, and holds the hydrating root on Reagent if the page-assembly they need is missing.

evals.name: r-decline-reagent-introspection
evals.prompt:
Convert this view to Freehand:
(defn thing [] [:div (str (r/current-component))])
expectations: Declines — Reagent component-introspection / scheduler calls have no Freehand equivalent (MIG-35).
Warns that r/current-component still COMPILES after conversion and fails or returns nil at runtime, so no build gate catches it.

Keeps the view on Reagent, or restructures away from the introspection (props and :children are already the props map the view receives); does NOT equate the schedulers r/next-tick / r/after-render with a registered behavior — different phase, frequency and owner.

evals.name: m-negative-bare-symbol-not-spread
evals.prompt:
Migrate to Freehand:
(defn item [t] [:li t])
(defn lst [ts] [:ul (for [t ts] ^{:key t} [item t])])
expectations: Converts item and lst to v/defview and moves ^{:key t} to a :key prop (MIG-07): [item {:key t :t t}].
Does NOT treat the bare symbol child in [:li t] as a props map — `t` is content, never (v/spread t) (the bare-symbol trap).
Leaves the plain hiccup structure otherwise unchanged (MIG-14).

evals.name: d-mig18-handler-split
evals.prompt:
Migrate this view to Freehand:
(ns f (:require [re-frame.core :refer [dispatch]]))
(defn save-btn [] [:button {:on-click (fn [e] (.preventDefault e) (when @dirty? (dispatch [:save])))} "Save"])
expectations: Recognises MIG-18 — the handler is not one of the three clean shapes (mixed browser mechanic + guard + dispatch), so it is a judgment call, not an automatic lift.
Routes the guarded dispatch to v/event: its body names the outcome, and a nil return dispatches nothing — the guard expressed as data-with-a-filter.
Routes .preventDefault to the closed listener options map (:prevent-default true) rather than leaving it inside a closure.
Hoists the guard's read to render time and closes over the VALUE — a v/sub inside the callback would raise :rf.error/view-read-outside-render at click time.
Holds/decides the WHOLE view (the guard reads view-held state, coupling it to the MIG-16 state decision) — no half-migrated body.

evals.name: d-mig17-lifecycle-behavior-and-rehome
evals.prompt:
Migrate this Reagent Form-3 view to Freehand:
(ns app.editor (:require [reagent.core :as r] [reagent.dom :as rdom]))
(defn editor []
  (let [{:keys [dispatch]} (rf/capture-frame)]
    (r/create-class
     {:component-did-mount    (fn [this] (.focus (rdom/dom-node this)))
      :component-will-unmount (fn [_] (dispatch [:resource/release]))
      :reagent-render         (fn [] [editor-form])})))
expectations: Recognises MIG-17 Form-3 lifecycle and decomposes each body into host/DOM work vs domain work — a judgment call held WHOLE (cardinal rule 2), not an automatic rewrite.

Routes the host/DOM work (focus the node on mount) to a registered behavior — (v/defbehavior … {:connect … :disconnect …}) plus a [v/behavior {:use … :target … :config …} element] use site — and does NOT emit `effect` or `ref`, which Freehand does not export.
Chooses :timing deliberately: an initial focus ring that must exist at first paint declares :timing :layout; deferrable setup stays on the default :passive.
Recognises there is no dispatch-at-unmount: mount and unmount are host facts, and a behavior's :disconnect is not a place to smuggle a domain event.

Re-homes the unmount domain work (the [:resource/release] dispatch) OUT of the view — to whatever causally ends the resource (a route's :resources released on every route leave, a machine actor, or an app event that mints and an event that ends) — and names that owner for the author (cardinal rule 5).
Enumerates EVERY exit path when proposing the owner; an enumeration that covers save/delete but misses navigate-away is the classic leak.
Notes that Freehand exposes no view-tier frame handle, so the rf/capture-frame binding does not translate (MIG-31).

evals.name: d-mig17-measure-before-paint
evals.prompt:
Migrate this Reagent Form-3 view to Freehand:
(ns app.popover (:require [reagent.core :as r] [reagent.dom :as rdom]))
(defn popover [anchor]
  (r/create-class
   {:component-did-mount (fn [this] (place! (rdom/dom-node this) (measure anchor)))
    :reagent-render      (fn [a] [:div.popover])}))
expectations: Recognises MIG-17 Form-3 and that :component-did-mount here MEASURES then mutates BEFORE paint, so post-paint work would land a frame late and flicker.
Routes it to a registered behavior declaring :timing :layout — the pre-paint moment — and explains that :passive (the default) would flicker.
Does NOT emit ui/ref, a React hook, or any use-layout-effect form: Freehand exports no ref and no hook tier, and the behavior is handed the node it decorates.

Puts the anchor geometry inputs in :config as DATA — a node, a ref, a callback or a preconstructed host instance in :config is refused on both hosts — and re-feeds on change through :update, which runs only when the committed :config moves by rf=.
Holds/decides the WHOLE view (cardinal rule 2) rather than half-migrating it.

evals.name: d-foreign-react-component-inward
evals.prompt:
Migrate this view to Freehand:
(ns app.picker (:require ["react-datepicker" :default DatePicker]))
(defn booking [] [:div [:> DatePicker {:selected @(subscribe [:date]) :onChange #(dispatch [:date/set %])}]])
expectations: Does NOT blanket-decline as a foreign-React reject: the React host boundary has landed inward, so this is a judgment-flavoured conversion (MIG-09/10), not a wait.

Recognises the reshape — a bare React COMPONENT at a vector head ([:> DatePicker …]) is still illegal, so it CREATES a React element (react/createElement, a JSX helper, or reagent.core/as-element) and places that ELEMENT in a CHILD position, never at the head.

Crosses the foreign props as ordinary React props on the created element: the fn-valued :onChange and the :selected value are foreign React props, NOT Freehand projection markers or a v/event site, and the @(subscribe [:date]) deref becomes a render-time (v/sub [:date]) read feeding :selected.

States the limit that decides the call: the JVM structural renderer accepts no React elements, so the region around the foreign child is browser-only and cannot be covered by a t/render structural test — assert the Freehand parts structurally, cover the integration in a mounted browser test.
Decides the WHOLE view with the author (cardinal rule 2); does NOT invent a Freehand host descriptor or wrapper verb for the foreign head.

evals.name: r-trusted-markup-holds
evals.prompt:
Migrate this to Freehand:
(defn article-body [html] [:div.body {:dangerouslySetInnerHTML {:__html html}}])
expectations: Declines (MIG-34): :dangerouslySetInnerHTML is refused and no trusted-markup verb is exported, so the view stays on Reagent.
Does NOT reach for v/markup — v/markup crosses a HICCUP VALUE into a compiled body (MIG-30); it does not parse or inject an HTML string, and using it here would render the markup as text.
Does not invent v/html or any other unexported form (cardinal rule 6).

evals.name: m-mount-and-frame-preflight
evals.prompt:
Migrate the boot for this app to Freehand:
(ns app.core (:require [reagent.dom :as rdom] [re-frame.core :as rf] [re-frame.adapter.reagent :as ra]))
(defn init! []
  (rf/init! ra/adapter)
  (rf/dispatch-sync [:app/init])
  (rdom/render [app] (js/document.getElementById "root")))
expectations: Rewrites to (v/mount [app {}] el {:frame {:id :app :initial-events [[:app/init]]}}) — the :frame opt is the preflight and drains before React sees anything (MIG-15).
States that Freehand needs no adapter install of its own, and that (rf/init! ra/adapter) is deleted only when the page's LAST Reagent root converts — confirming the root inventory with the author.
Deletes the React-18 create-root / defonce-atom dance if present: v/mount is idempotent per root, which is the hot-reload path.
Does not seed with dispatch-sync after mount when preflight can do it before paint.

evals.name: d-mig28-spread-vs-spread-safe
evals.prompt:
Migrate this reusable control to Freehand:
(defn text-field [attrs draft on-input]
  [:input (merge attrs {:type "text" :value (:title draft) :on-change on-input})])
expectations: Recognises MIG-28 and picks between the two forwards rather than reaching for the first one: (v/spread base overrides) is the visible-cost forward, (v/spread-safe owned caller) is the bounded one.

Chooses v/spread-safe here, because the control owns :value and its handler and must keep them: the deny law bars :key, :ref, :value, :checked and the component's own on-* families from `caller`, in every build.
Puts the owned props in the `owned` argument and the consumer's map in `caller`, and notes survivors fold under owned props with :class composing.
Respells :on-change/:onChange to the kebab spelling and lifts the handler where MIG-04/05 applies.
